section_summary.extract_value: The Discussion summarizes a single-study model examining interpersonal (adult attachment, caregiver eating messages) and intrapersonal (maladaptive/discrepancy and adaptive perfectionism) predictors of body appreciation and how body appreciation relates to intuitive eating and depressive symptoms. Body appreciation mediated relations between some predictors (e.g., discrepancy perfectionism, attachment anxiety, restrictive/critical caregiver messages) and intuitive eating but did not uniquely predict depressive symptoms; discrepancy perfectionism, attachment anxiety, and high standards perfectionism were unique predictors of depressive symptoms. The section does not report sample size, demographics (e.g., percent white, mean age), BMI measurement, or the specific body appreciation instrument used in the provided text.
section_summary.evidence_source: "In this study, we explored a model including potential interpersonal (i.e., adult attachment, caregiver eating messages) and intrapersonal (i.e., maladaptive and adaptive perfectionism) barriers and facilitators to body appreciation as well as body appreciation's ties to two indices of well-being (i.e., depressive symptoms and intuitive eating)." and "Overall, this model provided a good foundation from which to understand college women's body appreciation and its connection to intuitive eating."
